name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q01 - Priestley and Ingenhousz early photosynthesis experiments

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Joseph Priestley hypothesised that plants restore to the air whatever breathing animals and burning candles remove.

Statement II: Jan Ingenhousz showed that sunlight is essential to the plant process that purifies air and that only the green parts of plants release oxygen.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Early experiments in the late eighteenth century established the roles of air, sunlight, and green plant parts in gas exchange during photosynthesis.

Step 2: Evaluation
Joseph Priestley (1770) observed in bell jar experiments that a mint plant kept a mouse alive and a candle burning, leading to his hypothesis that plants restore to the air whatever breathing animals and burning candles remove. Jan Ingenhousz later placed a similar setup in dark and sunlight and used an aquatic plant to show that sunlight is essential and only green parts form oxygen bubbles.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q02 - Chloroplast membrane system and stroma reactions

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: The membrane system of the chloroplast is responsible for trapping light energy and synthesising ATP and NADPH.

Statement II: Enzymatic reactions in the chloroplast stroma are directly driven by photons to synthesise sugar from \(\mathrm{CO_2}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Within the chloroplast, light reactions occur in the membranous system (grana and stroma lamellae), while carbon reactions occur in the stroma.

Step 2: Evaluation
The membrane system traps light energy and synthesises ATP and NADPH; hence, the claim about the membrane system is correct. In contrast, the enzymatic reactions in the stroma that synthesise sugar are not directly light-driven (though they depend on ATP and NADPH from light reactions); hence, the claim that stromal reactions are directly driven by photons is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim regarding the membrane system is correct, whereas the claim regarding stromal reactions being directly photon-driven is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q03 - Chlorophyll a and accessory pigments

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Chlorophyll a appears yellow-green in a paper chromatogram and functions only as an accessory pigment.

Statement II: Accessory pigments such as carotenoids and xanthophylls absorb light, transfer energy to chlorophyll a, and protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Four pigments are separated from leaves by paper chromatography: chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, xanthophylls, and carotenoids.

Step 2: Evaluation
Chlorophyll a appears bright or blue-green (not yellow-green, which is chlorophyll b) and is the chief photosynthetic pigment, not an accessory pigment; thus, that claim is incorrect. Carotenoids, xanthophylls, and chlorophyll b are accessory pigments that absorb light across a wider wavelength range, transfer energy to chlorophyll a, and protect it from photo-oxidation; thus, that claim is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim about chlorophyll a is incorrect, whereas the claim about accessory pigments is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q04 - Naming and reaction centres of PS I and PS II

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Photosystem I and Photosystem II are named in the sequence in which they function during the light reaction.

Statement II: The reaction centre chlorophyll a in PS I is P680, whereas in PS II it is P700.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Photosystems I and II are distinct light-harvesting complexes with different reaction-centre absorption maxima.

Step 2: Evaluation
PS I and PS II are named in the sequence of their discovery, not the sequence in which they function (PS II functions before PS I in non-cyclic flow); thus, the naming claim is incorrect. Moreover, the reaction centre of PS I has an absorption peak at \(700\ \text{nm}\) (P700) and that of PS II has an absorption maximum at \(680\ \text{nm}\) (P680), so reversing them makes the second claim incorrect as well.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q05 - Z-scheme electron transport and water splitting site

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: In the Z-scheme, electrons excited from PS II are passed downhill through an electron transport system consisting of cytochromes to PS I.

Statement II: The water-splitting complex is associated with PS II and is physically located on the inner side of the thylakoid membrane.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Non-cyclic electron transport transfers electrons from water through PS II, cytochromes, and PS I to \(\mathrm{NADP^+}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
Electrons excited from P680 in PS II are picked up by a primary acceptor and move downhill on a redox potential scale through a cytochrome electron transport chain to PS I. Simultaneously, the water-splitting complex associated with PS II is located on the inner (lumen) side of the thylakoid membrane, releasing protons and \(\mathrm{O_2}\) into the lumen while supplying electrons to PS II.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q06 - Cyclic photophosphorylation in stroma lamellae

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Cyclic photophosphorylation results only in the synthesis of ATP and not of \(\mathrm{NADPH + H^+}\).

Statement II: Stroma lamellae membranes possess abundant PS II and NADP reductase enzyme.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cyclic photophosphorylation occurs when only PS I is functional, such as in stroma lamellae.

Step 2: Evaluation
During cyclic electron flow, excited electrons cycle back to PS I through the electron transport chain, synthesising only ATP without \(\mathrm{NADPH + H^+}\); hence, the first claim is correct. However, stroma lamellae membranes lack both PS II and the NADP reductase enzyme (which are present in grana lamellae); hence, the second claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim about cyclic photophosphorylation products is correct, whereas the claim about stroma lamellae composition is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q07 - Chemiosmotic proton gradient and ATP synthase

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: During the light reaction, protons accumulate in the chloroplast stroma, causing a measurable decrease in stromal pH.

Statement II: Breakdown of the proton gradient through the \(\mathrm{CF_0}\) channel provides energy for a conformational change in \(\mathrm{CF_1}\) to synthesise ATP.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Chemiosmosis in chloroplasts couples a transmembrane proton gradient across the thylakoid membrane to ATP synthesis.

Step 2: Evaluation
During light reactions, protons accumulate in the thylakoid lumen (decreasing luminal pH) while stromal protons decrease; thus, the claim of proton accumulation in the stroma is incorrect. As protons diffuse back to the stroma through \(\mathrm{CF_0}\), the energy released causes a conformational change in \(\mathrm{CF_1}\), synthesising ATP; thus, the second claim is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim about stromal proton accumulation is incorrect, whereas the claim about \(\mathrm{CF_0}\)-\(\mathrm{CF_1}\) ATP synthesis is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q08 - Melvin Calvin discovery and primary CO2 acceptor

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Melvin Calvin used \(^{14}\text{C}\) in algal photosynthesis studies to show that the first \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) fixation product is the 4-carbon oxaloacetic acid.

Statement II: The primary \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) acceptor in the Calvin cycle is a 2-carbon aldose sugar.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Melvin Calvin elucidated the \(\mathrm{C_3}\) pathway using radioactive \(^{14}\text{C}\) in algae.

Step 2: Evaluation
Calvin discovered that the first \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) fixation product was a 3-carbon organic acid, 3-phosphoglyceric acid (PGA), not 4-carbon oxaloacetic acid; thus, the first claim is incorrect. Furthermore, the primary \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) acceptor was found to be the 5-carbon ketose sugar ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP), not a 2-carbon compound; thus, the second claim is also incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q09 - Universality and carboxylation of the Calvin cycle

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: The Calvin pathway occurs in all photosynthetic plants, regardless of whether they have \(\mathrm{C_3}\) or \(\mathrm{C_4}\) pathways.

Statement II: Carboxylation of RuBP catalysed by RuBisCO results in the formation of two molecules of 3-PGA.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The Calvin cycle is the universal biosynthetic pathway for sugar synthesis in photosynthetic plants.

Step 2: Evaluation
Both \(\mathrm{C_3}\) and \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants (and other photosynthetic plants) use the Calvin pathway to synthesise sugars. In its first stage (carboxylation), RuBisCO catalyses the combination of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) with 5-carbon RuBP to form two molecules of 3-carbon 3-phosphoglycerate (3-PGA).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q10 - ATP and NADPH stoichiometry in Calvin cycle

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Formation of one molecule of glucose requires \(6\) turns of the Calvin cycle, consuming \(18\text{ ATP}\) and \(12\text{ NADPH}\).

Statement II: Each turn of the Calvin cycle consumes \(2\text{ ATP}\) in the regeneration step and \(1\text{ ATP}\) in the reduction step.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each turn of the Calvin cycle fixes one \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) molecule using \(3\text{ ATP}\) and \(2\text{ NADPH}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
For \(6\) turns (one glucose molecule), total consumption is \(6 \times 3 = 18\text{ ATP}\) and \(6 \times 2 = 12\text{ NADPH}\); thus, the overall stoichiometry claim is correct. However, per \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) fixed, \(2\text{ ATP}\) (along with \(2\text{ NADPH}\)) are used in reduction and \(1\text{ ATP}\) is used in RuBP regeneration, not the reverse; thus, the per-step ATP allocation claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The overall glucose stoichiometry claim is correct, whereas the per-step ATP allocation claim is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q11 - Enzyme distribution and bundle sheath cells in C4 plants

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: In \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants, mesophyll cells are rich in RuBisCO and lack PEPcase.

Statement II: Bundle sheath cells in \(\mathrm{C_4}\) leaves have thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and lack intercellular spaces.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
\(\mathrm{C_4}\) leaves exhibit Kranz anatomy with distinct enzyme compartmentalisation between mesophyll and bundle sheath cells.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants, mesophyll cells contain PEPcase and lack RuBisCO (whereas bundle sheath cells are rich in RuBisCO and lack PEPcase); thus, the first claim is incorrect. Bundle sheath cells indeed possess thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange, numerous chloroplasts, and no intercellular spaces; thus, the second claim is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim about mesophyll enzyme content is incorrect, whereas the claim about bundle sheath cell structure is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q12 - Calvin cycle location and decarboxylation in C4 plants

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: In \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants, the Calvin cycle takes place in both mesophyll cells and bundle sheath cells.

Statement II: Decarboxylation of \(\mathrm{C_4}\) acids in bundle sheath cells releases \(\mathrm{O_2}\) and a 5-carbon RuBP molecule.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants, the Calvin pathway is restricted to bundle sheath cells, which receive \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) via decarboxylation of \(\mathrm{C_4}\) acids.

Step 2: Evaluation
Because mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO, the Calvin cycle does not occur in mesophyll cells of \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants and takes place only in bundle sheath cells; thus, the first claim is incorrect. Moreover, decarboxylation of \(\mathrm{C_4}\) acids in bundle sheath cells releases \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) (not \(\mathrm{O_2}\)) and a 3-carbon molecule (not 5-carbon RuBP); thus, the second claim is also incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q13 - RuBisCO affinity and photorespiration products

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: RuBisCO has a much greater affinity for \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) than for \(\mathrm{O_2}\) when the \(\mathrm{CO_2} : \mathrm{O_2}\) ratio is nearly equal, and the binding is competitive.

Statement II: In \(\mathrm{C_3}\) plants, binding of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) to RuBisCO converts RuBP into one molecule of phosphoglycerate and one molecule of phosphoglycolate without synthesising sugars or ATP.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
RuBisCO is a bifunctional enzyme whose carboxylase versus oxygenase activity depends on competitive binding of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{O_2}\).

Step 2: Evaluation
When \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and \(\mathrm{O_2}\) concentrations are nearly equal, RuBisCO exhibits much higher affinity for \(\mathrm{CO_2}\), and the relative concentrations of the two gases govern competitive binding. In \(\mathrm{C_3}\) plants, oxygenation of RuBP produces one 3-carbon phosphoglycerate and one 2-carbon phosphoglycolate in the photorespiratory pathway, which neither synthesises sugars nor produces ATP or NADPH.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q14 - Photorespiration absence in C4 vs energetics in C3

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Photorespiration does not occur in \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants because decarboxylation of \(\mathrm{C_4}\) acids in bundle sheath cells increases intracellular \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) concentration at the RuBisCO site.

Statement II: In \(\mathrm{C_3}\) plants, the photorespiratory pathway synthesises ATP and NADPH while conserving fixed carbon.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Photorespiration is a wasteful oxygenation pathway present in \(\mathrm{C_3}\) plants and avoided in \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants, breakdown of \(\mathrm{C_4}\) acids in bundle sheath cells raises \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) concentration around RuBisCO, ensuring it acts as a carboxylase and preventing photorespiration; thus, the first claim is correct. In \(\mathrm{C_3}\) plants, photorespiration synthesises neither ATP nor NADPH and releases \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) with the utilisation of ATP; thus, the second claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim about \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants lacking photorespiration is correct, whereas the claim about photorespiration synthesising ATP and NADPH in \(\mathrm{C_3}\) plants is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q15 - Light saturation and CO2 saturation thresholds

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Light saturation occurs at \(50\%\) of full sunlight, making light the major limiting factor for open-field crops in nature.

Statement II: \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants show \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) saturation at about \(360\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\), whereas \(\mathrm{C_3}\) plants show saturation only beyond \(450\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Light intensity and \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) concentration exhibit distinct saturation points in \(\mathrm{C_3}\) and \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants.

Step 2: Evaluation
Light saturation occurs at \(10\%\) (not \(50\%\)) of full sunlight, so light is rarely a limiting factor in nature except for plants in shade or dense forests; thus, the light saturation claim is incorrect. At high light intensities, \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants saturate at about \(360\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\) while \(\mathrm{C_3}\) plants saturate only beyond \(450\ \mu\text{L L}^{-1}\); thus, the \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) saturation claim is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim about light saturation is incorrect, whereas the claim about \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) saturation in \(\mathrm{C_3}\) and \(\mathrm{C_4}\) plants is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CH13_STMT2_Q16 - Temperature control of dark reactions and water stress

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Statement I: Light reactions are strongly temperature-controlled, whereas enzymatic dark reactions are unaffected by temperature.

Statement II: Water stress increases photosynthetic rate by causing stomata to open wider and expanding leaf surface area.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Temperature and water availability influence photosynthesis through enzymatic activity and stomatal/leaf responses.

Step 2: Evaluation
Dark reactions, being enzymatic, are temperature-controlled, whereas light reactions are affected by temperature to a much lesser extent; thus, the first claim is incorrect. Water stress causes stomata to close (reducing \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) availability) and makes leaves wilt (reducing surface area and metabolic activity), thereby decreasing photosynthesis; thus, the second claim is also incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
